what_this_is: The wager census design section 10 gates grading on. Every DECLARED number below is transcribed from the design (section 6's per-market wager counts, section 10's two totals and its athlete-cluster figure, and the verdict table's store census) and was then reproduced exactly by the census. Every PINNED number was measured here and the design declares no counterpart, so it is a fingerprint that can only ever refuse -- it is not evidence of anything today, because it was measured and then compared with itself. `sources` says which each one is. Nothing here is a model constant and nothing here was fitted.

source.note: The store is a symlink into /Users/cooperross/Projects/cbb-betting-lab. Nothing else in this repository pins its contents, so without this digest the gate would certify whichever file the link pointed at.

notes.why_this_is_an_attribution_and_not_an_eq: Design section 10 asks for 261,870 to be reconciled against 257,474. Both are correct counts of the same rows under two spellings of the subject, so as an equality the gate can never open. What is gated instead is that every wager of the difference is NAMED: 4,396 collapses, 4,396 attributed to 64 casefold collision groups, residual exactly 0.
notes.neither_headline_is_a_grading_denominato: 261,870 and 257,474 both include the 723 wagers on player_first_basket and player_double_double, which are refused BY NAME. The priced denominators are 261,147 raw and 256,751 folded.
notes.no_subject_normalizer_is_declared: The design names the key and never says which spelling of `player` is the subject. Measured over five reasonable folds the denominator is 261,870 / 257,474 / 257,378 / 255,553 / 251,949. `declared_subject` is null until the lab declares one.
notes.no_athlete_level_denominator_exists_yet: The price store has no athlete_id column. The graded denominator is only knowable after section 7's R1 cascade runs and its refusals are removed; an approximation of R1's pre-match fold counts 251,949, at least 5,525 below the design's number.
notes.one_subject_is_ambiguous_and_no_fold_fix: 'Justin Moore', game_id 401604303, Villanova against Drexel, 2023-12-02, is two athlete_ids under one display name and is the only one of 9,098 quoted (game, folded-name) pairs the 2024 roster says covers more than one athlete. Section 7's R1 refuses more than one candidate rather than picking.
notes.the_shipped_collapse_uses_the_raw_spelli: stores._dedupe_value strips but does not casefold, so best_price_per_wager returns two rows for one athlete-line-side on the 4,396 collapsing keys; 3,959 of them carry more than one distinct american_odds. That is stores.py's own documented root-n defect arriving through the `player` field instead of the `book` field. Reported, not fixed here.
